# Why Dharma is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is no broken version of this name to repair. There is a record to preserve: **Dharma**, exactly as the scholarly convention supports it.

Dharma’s mythology is the epics’ moral machinery: the god of righteousness fathers the eldest Pāṇḍava, tests his devotees in disguise, and — in the Nala story — teaches dice to a king as the instrument of ruin. He has no cult-image because he is what every cult-image stands for; yet the tradition gave him a family and a biography.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Dharma
- **ASCII form:** dharma
- **Meaning:** "That which holds or sustains — law, duty, and righteousness; the moral and religious order that upholds the world (from √dhṛ, 'to hold, sustain')."
- **Domain of influence:** Law, Duty, Righteousness
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** धर्म
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 135 of 597

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/ˈdɑːrmə/` — “DAHR-muh”

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Dharma** lives at [/dharma/](/dharma/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/dharma/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/dharma/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/dharma/patterns/).

The displayed form is ASCII-equivalent.

## Where the Name Stood First

Dharma’s monuments are juridical: the edict-pillars of Aśoka, whose dhamma inscriptions are the oldest deciphered moral legislation on earth. His wheel crowns the Indian flag; his bull — the dharmavṛṣabha — kneels on the seal of the Republic. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Legal, Justice & Compliance** (that which holds — law, duty, and righteousness personified, father of the dharmarāja.); **Philosophy, Ethics & Standards** (the load-bearing concept of Indian ethics — svadharma as the standard every professional owes.); **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** (the god of righteousness to whom every tribunal answers — kingship's moral warrant.). The [Resonance File](/dharma/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
